articles.title: Midterms Could Swing on Diesel
articles.description: America runs on gasoline but the midterms could swing on diesel, Macquarie strategists warned.

articles.title: Woodside Posts Higher Quarterly Revenue
articles.description: 'Increased quarterly operating revenue reflected increased production and strong realized prices'.

articles.title: UK Greenlights $3B Jackdaw Gas Project
articles.description: UK Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh has greenlit the Jackdaw gas field.

articles.title: UK Government approves Jackdaw gas field in North Sea
articles.description: The UK government has approved plans for gas production at the Jackdaw field in the North Sea, with Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh authorising the regulator to grant consent for the project.

articles.title: Eni initiates start-up of Meleiha phase two gas project in Egypt
articles.description: Eni has commenced start-up operations at the Meleiha Phase 2 gas project in Egypt's Western Desert, advancing the creation of a new gas hub within the Merged Meleiha concession.

articles.title: Iran Intensifies Strikes on Ships
articles.description: At least 23 incidents involving ships attacked in or near Hormuz were logged in the first two weeks of October, with at least five reporting impacts to their engine rooms.

articles.title: Gulf Keystone and ShaMaran agree to $601m all-share merger
articles.description: Gulf Keystone Petroleum and ShaMaran Petroleum signed agreements to merge in an all-share transaction that values the latter at around $601m.

articles.title: Ukraine Welcomes Restored U.S. Intelligence Amid Russian Attacks
articles.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said he is thankful to the US as intelligence on Russian missile strikes "works now," after talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Oslo. Zelenskyy had previously said that Washington had temporarily paused some intelligence sharing with Kyiv before resuming it. "We are thankful that intelligence works.... I'm speaking about early warning, what is very important for our people, for children, adults, civilians, because we can hear when ballistic [missiles are] coming," Zelenskyy told reporters…

articles.title: Russia to Send First Diesel Tanker to U.S. on Thursday
articles.description: Russia will send its first diesel tanker to the US on Thursday under the agreement between Presidents Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters Wednesday, according to TASS and Prime. Novak did not name the port. He gave the tanker's displacement as 40,000 tons and said additional shipments will follow. "We will meet the United States' needs, to the extent of our capabilities," RIA quoted him as saying, via Reuters. Putin told US envoy Steve Witkoff on Wednesday that the first tanker, which he also put…

articles.title: Morgan Stanley: Global Fuel Market Will Stay Tight Through Mid-2027
articles.description: Global fuel markets are set to remain tight until at least the middle of next year as the second quarter of 2027 will see unusually high planned maintenance that refiners have deferred from this year, Morgan Stanley analysts say. Planned maintenance at refineries worldwide is set to peak at 3.4 million barrels per day (bpd) in the second quarter of 2027, as many facilities will be overdue for maintenance after currently running at maximum capacity utilization. In recent months, many refiners have postponed scheduled outages to keep fuels flowing…

articles.title: UK Approves Jackdaw Gas Field as Energy Crisis Deepens
articles.description: The UK government on Wednesday approved the long-delayed Jackdaw gas field in the first approval of a new North Sea project since the Iran war hiked energy prices. Jackdaw will start to supply gas to British homes and businesses from the end of this month, after the UK Energy Secretary agreed that the regulator can grant consent for gas to be produced at the field, Andy Burnham’s Labour government said in a statement. The Jackdaw project, led by Adura, the new company Shell and Equinor have created by merging their oil and gas assets in the…

articles.title: Goldman Sachs Warns of New Oil Price Shock as Tanker Rates Soar
articles.description: The average global freight rate to transport oil has surged to $20 per barrel from $3 per barrel last year as the Iran war and the Hormuz crisis have created a shipping crisis that’s unlikely to end soon, Goldman Sachs says. Oil shipping rates are set to remain elevated in the near term amid no end in sight to the Middle East crisis, with the massive surge in freight costs posing an upside risk to Goldman’s current baseline oil price forecast of $90 per barrel Brent crude at the end of this year, the bank’s analysts said in a…

articles.title: India’s Coal Crisis Deepens as Power Demand Surges
articles.description: Indian power generators are bracing for a coal supply squeeze, with half of the country’s coal power plant fleet operating with critically low stocks, Reuters has reported, citing higher than usual demand for electricity because of warmer than usual weather for this time of year. As many as 96 coal power plants in the country only have stocks for three days of consumption, the publication wrote, citing data from India’s Central Electricity Authority. This is up from 60 power plants operating with critically low stocks as of mid-September.…

articles.title: Trump Administration Pushes Refiners to Boost Diesel Output as Prices Soar
articles.description: The U.S. Department of Energy has called on refiners to ramp up their diesel fuel production further, Reuters has reported, citing two high-ranking officials from the department. There are talks ongoing with refiners both in the United States and abroad, the report said. This is the latest move on the part of the federal government to push diesel prices down from all-time highs, with the national average stuck above $6 per gallon. The report follows a decision by President Trump to waive sanctions on Russian exports in a bid to secure additional…

articles.title: Oil Prices Climb Above $110 as Middle East Supply Fears Persist
articles.description: Crude oil prices ticked higher earlier today, extending gains from Tuesday as traders continued to worry about the stability of flows out of the Middle East. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $110.30 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $99.12 per barrel, both up by over 1% from Tuesday. The latest inventory report out of the U.S. contributed to the bullish sentiment with another sizable draw estimated for last week. The rally also comes despite a Wall Street Journal report from Tuesday that said oil flows out of the Middle…

articles.title: Oil Slips as Iran Talks Fuel Volatility
articles.description: Oil retreated from five-month highs amid uncertain Iran negotiations and volatile trading.

articles.title: Halliburton Sees Years of Growth as Mideast Rebuilds
articles.description: Halliburton Co. is predicting years of growing demand for oil field services as nations in the Middle East rebuild energy assets and infrastructure.

articles.title: How Bad Would It Get If China Blocks Rare Earths to America?
articles.description: Taiwan is the next pressure point that will test China's weaponization of rare earth metals. When Japan indicated it would not remain neutral in a Taiwan conflict, Beijing responded by sharply restricting exports of several heavy rare earth materials, including dysprosium and terbium. Japan was the test case. With U.S.-China tensions escalating, a confrontation could likely lead to an immediate blockade of Chinese rare earths to American markets, pressuring U.S. defense without firing a single shot. From a defense perspective, it would be disastrous…

articles.title: Petrobras' Deepwater Push Sets Off a Race for Offshore Vessels
articles.description: Recently, we reported that the Middle East conflict and subsequent closure of the Strait of Hormuz has triggered an unprecedented spike in freight and shipping rates, with Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) spot rates now exceeding $1 million per day. The sharp spike is now reshaping oil flows and forcing producers to cut prices in a bid to help buyers offset extra transport costs. The situation is a little different in Brazil, where the offshore sector is facing a potential vessel shortage as demand outruns supply amid the offshore oil boom, positioning…

articles.title: Mexico Poised to Approve $12.5 Billion in Renewable Energy Projects
articles.description: Mexico’s state power utility is today set to greenlight as many as 60 alternative energy projects, most of them solar, that should add 8.2 GW in new generation capacity to the country’s total, according to an unnamed source that spoke to Bloomberg. The total investment in these projects could reach $12.5 billion. The projects set to be approved by the Federal Electricity Commission today may end up being fewer than 60, another source told Bloomberg, also wishing to remain unnamed. However many do get approved, they will go towards reaching…

articles.title: Europe’s Power Demand Returns to Growth
articles.description: Despite weakening industrial activity and high energy costs, European electricity demand is bucking years of flailing power consumption. Rising electrification rates and the data center boom are the key drivers of this new trend in Europe’s power demand, which is set to gather momentum in the coming years amid the EU’s energy transition and the global AI boom. Europe’s electricity demand growth is nowhere near the pace seen in the United States and China in recent years, but it’s a marked shift nevertheless, after years…

articles.title: Energy Costs Are Driving U.S. Inflation, and Wages Aren't Keeping Up
articles.description: Inflation rates remain blistering high across the United States. The Bureau of Labor Statistics’s most recent Consumer Price Index, released last week, revealed numbers that were higher than most projections, indicating long-term pain for consumers and a nightmare election cycle for Donald Trump. And the reason for all of it is huge and persistent volatility in global oil and gas markets. The October 14 Consumer Price Index showed that overall, prices for goods and services across the United States have risen 3.7 percent over the last…

articles.title: API: Crude, Product Inventories Continue to Draw
articles.description: The American Petroleum Institute (API) estimated that crude oil inventories in the United States fell by 4.93 million barrels in the week ending October 16. In the week prior, US crude oil inventories fell by a staggering 11.12 million barrels. Commercial crude oil inventories excluding the SPR have lost more than 56 million barrels over the last 27 weeks, but US crude inventories are still only 5 million barrels below where they were at the beginning of the year, according to API data, kept in check in part thanks to draws from the SPR. For the…

articles.title: From pilot to fleet: Automa 2026 on scaling digital offshore
articles.description: Automa 2026 in Amsterdam brought operators, EPCs and technology providers together to discuss scaling offshore digitalisation.
